Going Under (Aggro Crab, 2020)

A satirical dungeon-crawler about failed tech startups, whose characters and office spaces take the style’s colors and shapes into 3D.

Source
Steam: Going Under
Creator
Aggro Crab (developer); Team17 (publisher)
Made
Released 24 September 2020
Style
Corporate Memphis (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Satirical, bright, chaotic
Evidence
Inspected two 1920 × 1080 screenshots from the Steam store API (a boss fight and the company lobby). No image is stored.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Steam describes it as “a satirical dungeon crawler about exploring the cursed ruins of failed tech startups”, with the player as an unpaid intern in the city of Neo-Cascadia. Developer Aggro Crab, publisher Team17, released 24 September 2020. Steam.

Reviews and essays describe its art as a parody of Corporate Memphis, for example Merry-Go-Round Magazine.

Observed

  • The lobby screenshot shows pink and peach walls, a green floor with orange paths, and long yellow and purple pill-shaped benches.
  • Rounded teal trees stand in violet pots on red bases; giant soda cans float over a fountain.
  • The boss screenshot shows a violet brick room with a zig-zag stripe, and a large monster with blue arms and an orange body.
  • Surfaces carry a brushed, speckled texture and soft 3D shading.

Why it belongs

Going Under shows how recognizable the style became by 2020: a game could use its palette and props as shorthand for startup culture and make fun of it.

Borrow

For a satirical or self-aware brand, keep the style’s palette and props but add texture to signal distance from it.
